title: Capacity-aware staggered maintenance orchestrator for dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a maintenance orchestrator that schedules and executes node-level maintenance (OS patching, driver updates, node reboots, and capacity rotation) in dedicated fleets while preserving throughput guarantees and minimizing customer impact. The orchestrator will be capacity- and traffic-aware, support staggered drains across racks/zones, expose configuration for autoscaling interaction, and provide observability and rollback controls.
background: Current maintenance operations are largely manual and use broad drain windows which cause capacity cliffs for some customers during peak traffic.

We need a system that coordinates maintenance with autoscaling, SLOs, and model routing policies so that reserved throughput is preserved for committed customers and best-effort workloads are deprioritized.
Existing tickets (e.g., earlier node-drain/upgrade work) addressed parts of this flow; this ticket unifies scheduling, pacing, and policy integration into an orchestrator component.
goals: Ensure >99.95% of customer routes maintain their committed throughput during scheduled maintenance windows for Dedicated pools with reserved capacity.
Automate staggered drains by rack/zone and space them based on predicted headroom and current traffic.
Integrate with autoscaling policies so temporary burst scaling can be triggered pre-maintenance and scaled down after completion.
Provide runtime controls: pause, accelerate, abort maintenance; and a safe rollback path for failed node upgrades.
Emit observability events and dashboards: maintenance progress, per-route request latency percentiles, evictions, and recovered capacity timelines.
acceptance_criteria: Can schedule a maintenance job targeting a subset of nodes defined by label/rack/zone with a maintenance window and policy (aggressive | conservative | SLO-aware).

During simulated maintenance on a canary fleet, reserved-capacity customers see no more than 5% degradation in 99th percentile latency and no throughput loss beyond their SLA for longer than the configured window.
Autoscaler integration: the orchestrator can request a temporary scale-up and then release extra capacity after maintenance completes.
All maintenance actions are recorded in audit logs and surfaced in the Console with per-node timeline and linked GitHub PRs or runbooks.
Feature gated behind a runtime feature flag and enabled by default only for internal canary pools.
implementation_notes: Controller design: build a Kubernetes-style controller in the control plane that manages MaintenanceJob CRD-like objects (internal datastore, not Kubernetes API), tracking state machine: SCHEDULED -> PREPARE -> DRAINING -> MAINTAIN -> VALIDATE -> COMPLETE/ROLLED_BACK.
Headroom prediction: use 1h and 6h traffic baselines plus current autoscaler metrics to compute safe concurrency of concurrent drains per zone.
Drain pacing: implement token-bucket pacing where tokens represent node-drain permits; replenish rate computed from predicted headroom and reserved throughput commitments.
KV cache preservation: support a two-phase drain where serving processes checkpoint/serialize model KV caches for fastest warm starts on node rejoin; fallback to cold-start if checkpoint fails.
Routing policies: consult per-route priority metadata (reserved | best-effort | background) and avoid evicting routes marked reserved unless explicitly allowed.
Upgrade strategy: support live kernel/driver pre-checks, rolling in-place upgrades, and an optional hot-swap path using standby nodes from Dedicated burst capacity pools.
Observability: emit events to Console backend; new dashboards: maintenance-ops, maintenance-impact-by-customer, drain-pacing-utilization.
tasks: Design: final API and state machine (owner: Diego) - 2d
Prototype: control plane controller and maintenance job datastore - 5d
Integrate: autoscaler API hooks and burst-request flow - 4d
Agent work: node agent support for two-phase drain and KV cache checkpoint - 6d
Console: UI for scheduling, progress, and abort controls - 5d
E2E tests: simulated traffic harness and canary runs - 4d
Docs & runbooks: public docs + internal runbook for SEs - 3d
rollout_plan: Feature flagged rollout: internal canary cluster -> selected Dedicated customers (opt-in only) -> gradual opt-in to all Dedicated pools.
Phase 1 (canary): run on non-customer-facing pools for 2 weeks, collect metrics and fix regressions.
Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 3 low-impact Dedicated customers, run one maintenance exercise with full monitoring and SE on-call support.
Phase 3 (ga): enable for all Dedicated pools behind opt-in and then default-enable after 60 days with documented behavior.
Safety: abort/rollback triggers include >10% sustained increase in 95/99 p99 latency for reserved routes or evictions above threshold.
tests: Unit tests for controller state transitions and pacing algorithm edge cases.
Integration tests: orchestrator <-> autoscaler API in staging cluster with synthetic traffic.
Chaos test: randomly fail node upgrade step and verify rollback completes and drained nodes rejoin with correct KV cache behavior.
Load test: simulate 95th/99th percentile traffic and validate reserved customers keep throughput during staged drains.
metrics_and_alerting: Number of concurrent drains per zone
Reserved-route error and latency deltas during maintenance
Autoscaler temporary capacity requested vs granted
risks: KV cache checkpointing may add latency or fail on certain model runtimes; need fallback and post-failure analysis.
Incorrect headroom prediction could cause simultaneous capacity loss for multiple customers if fleets are correlated.
Autoscaler race: orchestrator requests burst capacity but autoscaler fails to provision in time leading to dropped requests.
mitigations: Start with conservative drain pacing and progressively loosen based on empirical safe headroom observed in canaries.
Add circuit breakers: if autoscaler does not grant burst within timeout, pause maintenance and notify on-call.
Run KV checkpoint experiments on a range of model sizes and versions; implement exponential backoff and circuit open for repeated failures.
